key_insight: UniIntervene++ adaptively decides when to let a robot act alone, when to intervene, and when to hand control back, so intervention stays matched to the policy’s changing competence during online RL.
engineering_relevance: For real-world robot learning, it offers a practical way to cut human oversight while preserving safety and improving sample efficiency as policies improve.
method: Unifies the RL policy, trajectory correction, and task-structured CodePolicy as Options in a semi-Markov decision process.
Learns option values online to choose between autonomous execution and heterogeneous assisted behaviors.
Periodically probes the policy with unassisted rollouts and uses coupled experience learning so assistance improves future policy and intervention decisions.
evidence_signal: Across five real-world manipulation tasks, it reached 89.67% average success, beat all baselines by at least 6 points, and reduced human intervention to 0.77% (at least 94.6% lower than the best baseline).
watch_item: Because it relies on periodic unassisted probing, poor probing design or safety-critical tasks could still incur risk if the policy is currently too weak.
paper_title: UniIntervene++: An Adaptive Intervention Agent for Efficient Real-World Reinforcement Learning
